subject: Finova — Performance SLOs & Multi-region routing (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finova.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-02T14:10:00Z
Subject: Finova — Performance SLOs & Multi-region routing (post-call recap)

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Key performance targets we captured (please correct me if I misremember):
- Latency: p95 <= 150 ms for short responses (<= 256 tokens); p95 <= 300 ms for long responses (<= 2048 tokens). Target p50 ~ 40–60 ms for short responses.
- Throughput: baseline sustained ~500 req/s, peak bursts up to ~1,500 req/s (very short windows).
- Concurrency: per-customer concurrent streams expected ~800–1,000; weekend/marketing peaks could push to ~1,500.
- Streaming: partial token streaming required for UI (SSE or chunked HTTP). Need sub-200 ms first-byte for streaming in US, sub-250 ms EU, sub-350 ms APAC as a starting objective.
- Regional routing & data residency: all EU requests must be routed to EU-hosted inference and logs kept in EU; APAC requests should be routed to an APAC region (data residency for APAC is optional but preferred).

Security & compliance items mentioned: SOC 2 evidence, network egress controls, and KMS-backed encryption for customer keys. You flagged the need to include audit logs showing routing decisions and per-request metadata.

Action items / next steps:
1) Redwood to produce an SLO worksheet with recommended configuration (models, quantization suggestions, batch size, KV caching) and estimated token/unit cost — target deliverable: SLO_worksheet.xlsx (attached). (Owner: me)
2) Schedule a 30–45m technical review with Redwood infra (Aditya) to validate regional routing, failover / fallback policies, and streaming tests. (Owner: Finova + Redwood)
3) Finova to share a sample traffic profile (QPS, median/95th token lengths, concurrency windows) and any procurement timeline. (Owner: Finova)

Proposed timeline: SLO worksheet by EOD 2026-06-03; technical review 2026-06-04 / 06-05 depending on availability.

If that aligns, I’ll send calendar invites and attach the worksheet.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: SLO_worksheet.xlsx

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency targets — the p95 numbers look reasonable. For streaming-first-byte targets, could we aim for p95 first-byte <= 120 ms in US and <= 180 ms in EU for our higher-tier customers? We understand APAC will be higher but want to constrain to p95 <= 300 ms if possible.
2) Concurrency — our immediate need is 800 sustained concurrent user streams (chat sessions). Peak concurrency 1,500 for short bursts (marketing-driven).
3) Throughput — 500 req/s baseline is correct. For verification, we’ll provide a 7-day sample of traffic (QPS per minute and token-length distribution).
4) Data residency — EU-only processing for EU customers is mandatory; APAC: we’re evaluating whether APAC residency is required for regulated markets (we’ll confirm).

Procurement note: we’re wrapping up vendor comparisons this quarter. If we can validate routing and the EU residency constraint, procurement can move fast.

Can Aditya advise on whether Redwood supports region-based model pinning + automatic fallback to nearest compatible variant (for cost/latency tradeoffs)? Also, we want to see how KV prefix caching impacts p95 for short responses.

Thanks — Alex

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Finova — Performance SLOs & Multi-region routing (post-call recap)

Alex / Marissa — quick technical notes ahead of the call. Short answers: yes, Redwood supports region-based model pinning + automatic fallback; KV prefix caching materially reduces p95 for short responses; streaming via SSE is supported and we also support HTTP chunked streaming for clients that need it.

Technical details / expectations:
- Regional routing: we recommend routing at the edge (regional ingress) with per-tenant routing policy enforced in the control plane. EU traffic -> EU-only inference cluster (data residency), APAC traffic -> APAC cluster, US traffic -> US cluster. We can also enforce log retention regionally and KMS key scoping per region.
- Model pinning & fallback: you can pin a model version per region. If capacity is constrained, the control plane can fallback to a compatible quantized variant in < 2s for cold start fallback, or < 200–400 ms for warm instances (depends on KV cache warmness).
- Expected latency numbers (empirical on our standard configurations):
  * US (g4dn-like equiv): p50 ~ 35–60 ms, p95 ~ 80–140 ms for short (<256 tokens) with KV caching + batching tuned for SLO.
  * EU (v3-like equiv): p50 ~ 50–80 ms, p95 ~ 120–200 ms.
  * APAC (regional cloud): p50 ~ 70–110 ms, p95 ~ 180–320 ms.
- Throughput/concurrency guidance: a single dedicated GPU slice can sustain ~250–400 short-response req/s depending on batching window and model variant. For your 500 req/s baseline we recommend 2–3 GPU slices distributed across regions with autoscaling configured for burst capacity. For peak bursts (1,500 req/s) plan for burst autoscaling and an additional 4–6 slices for sub-minute bursts.
- Streaming: recommend SSE for fastest first-byte delivery. We measure first-byte latencies roughly 30–50% lower for SSE vs long-polling; chunk sizes ~32–64 tokens balance interactivity and overhead.
- KV cache: expect p95 improvements of 30–60% on short responses where prefixes are common. Cache hit-rate assumptions drive cost savings — provide your sample traffic and we’ll model expected hit rates.

Attachments: network_traceroute.txt (sample traceroute to EU and APAC egress points)

I’ll be on the technical review on 2026-06-04 at 10:00 PST — feel free to share the traffic sample here or via the Drive link.
